source.text_it: Nel caso di infortunio con frattura della base cranica si deve tamponare l'emorragia dall'orecchio

records.localized_text: For a skull-base fracture, bleeding from the ear must be plugged.

source.text_it: La posizione laterale di sicurezza facilita la respirazione e la fuoriuscita di eventuali liquidi presenti in bocca

records.localized_text: The recovery position facilitates breathing and drainage of any fluids from the mouth.

source.text_it: In caso di trauma cranico, il soccorritore deve chiamare l'ambulanza anche se l'infortunato non lo ritiene necessario

records.localized_text: In case of head trauma, the rescuer must call an ambulance even if the injured person thinks it unnecessary.

source.text_it: Se l'infortunato è incosciente ma respira è necessario porlo nella posizione laterale di sicurezza

records.localized_text: If an injured person is unconscious but breathing, place them in the recovery position.

source.text_it: La posizione laterale di sicurezza è la posizione più appropriata per un infortunato incosciente che respira

records.localized_text: The recovery position is most appropriate for an unconscious person who is breathing.

source.text_it: La posizione laterale di sicurezza accelera il battito cardiaco

records.localized_text: The recovery position speeds up the heartbeat.

source.text_it: L' infortunato con trauma cranico si soccorre sdraiandolo sulla schiena con le gambe alzate

records.localized_text: An injured person with head trauma is helped by lying them on their back with legs raised.

source.text_it: Un infortunato è in stato di shock quando il sangue arriva poco al cervello e al cuore

records.localized_text: An injured person is in shock when too little blood reaches the brain and heart.

source.text_it: Se l'infortunato è in stato di shock occorre porlo supino a terra e alzargli le gambe

records.localized_text: If an injured person is in shock, lay them on their back on the ground and raise their legs.

source.text_it: Un'abbondante perdita di sangue può provocare lo stato di shock

records.localized_text: Heavy blood loss can cause shock.

source.text_it: Un sintomo dello stato di shock è la condizione di confusione mentale

records.localized_text: Mental confusion is a symptom of shock.

source.text_it: Se l'infortunato è in stato di shock presenta battiti del cuore deboli ma frequenti

records.localized_text: An injured person in shock has a weak but rapid heartbeat.

source.text_it: Un infortunato è in stato di shock quando ha un marcato rossore del viso

records.localized_text: An injured person is in shock when their face is markedly flushed.

source.text_it: Un infortunato è in stato di shock quando c'è una caduta della pressione arteriosa

records.localized_text: An injured person is in shock when blood pressure falls.

source.text_it: Un infortunato è in stato di shock quando ha riportato abrasioni superficiali

records.localized_text: An injured person is in shock when they have superficial abrasions.

source.text_it: Se l'infortunato è in stato di shock occorre somministrargli bevande alcoliche

records.localized_text: If an injured person is in shock, give them alcoholic drinks.

source.text_it: La posizione laterale di sicurezza funziona come stimolante in caso di shock

records.localized_text: The recovery position acts as a stimulant in shock.

source.text_it: Un infortunato è in stato di shock quando urla in continuazione

records.localized_text: An injured person is in shock when they scream continuously.

source.text_it: Se l'infortunato è in stato di shock è pallido, presenta brividi e manifesta sudorazione fredda

records.localized_text: An injured person in shock is pale, shivering and sweating coldly.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente stradale presenta una ferita sanguinante bisogna evitare infezioni usando insetticidi

records.localized_text: If a road accident victim has a bleeding wound, prevent infection using insecticides.

source.text_it: Nel caso di emorragia esterna venosa il soccorritore deve astenersi da qualsiasi intervento di primo soccorso, limitandosi a chiamare l'ambulanza

records.localized_text: For external venous bleeding, the rescuer must refrain from first aid and only call an ambulance.

source.text_it: Nel caso di una emorragia esterna arteriosa occorre comprimere con forza l'arteria principale interessata

records.localized_text: For external arterial bleeding, firmly compress the main affected artery.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente stradale presenta una ferita sanguinante bisogna evitare che il sangue sporchi la strada

records.localized_text: If a road accident victim has a bleeding wound, prevent blood from staining the road.

source.text_it: L'emorragia esterna arteriosa, pur se abbondante, non comporta pericolo di vita

records.localized_text: External arterial bleeding, even if heavy, is not life-threatening.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente presenta una ferita sanguinante occorre tener conto del rischio di infezione

records.localized_text: If an accident victim has a bleeding wound, consider the risk of infection.

rows.text: Do not plug the ear canal: cover the ear lightly and call emergency services. Blood or fluid from the ear after a head injury can signal serious injury.
evidence: St John Ambulance Canada, First Aid Reference Guide, bleeding from inside the ear and skull fracture: https://sja.ca/sites/default/files/2021-05/First%20aid%20reference%20guide_V4.1_Public.pdf — cover ear lightly; manage suspected skull fracture.
NHS, Head injury and concussion: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/head-injury-and-concussion/ — ear bleeding after head injury requires emergency help.

rows.text: The recovery position helps keep the airway clear and lets fluids drain from the mouth, reducing the risk of choking.
evidence: NHS Wales, First aid, Breathing and spinal injury: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — recovery position keeps airway clear; suspected spinal injury requires avoiding movement.

rows.text: A head injury can conceal damage that is not immediately apparent. After an accident or if there are danger signs, call emergency services even if the person downplays the problem.
evidence: Hato Hone St John, Head injuries: https://www.stjohn.org.nz/first-aid/first-aid-library/head-injuries/ — brain injury may not be immediately apparent.
NHS, Head injury and concussion: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/head-injury-and-concussion/ — high-speed road accident and danger signs warrant an ambulance.

rows.text: If the person is breathing normally, the recovery position helps keep the airway clear; call emergency services and monitor breathing. If you suspect a spinal injury, avoid moving them and follow the responders' instructions.
evidence: NHS Wales, First aid, Breathing and spinal injury: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — recovery position keeps airway clear; suspected spinal injury requires avoiding movement.

rows.text: For an unconscious person breathing normally, the recovery position helps keep the airway clear. If you suspect a spinal injury, avoid moving them and follow the responders' instructions.
evidence: NHS Wales, First aid, Breathing and spinal injury: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — recovery position keeps airway clear; suspected spinal injury requires avoiding movement.

rows.text: The recovery position keeps the airway clear and lets fluids drain from the mouth; it does not speed up the heart.
evidence: NHS Wales, First aid, Breathing and spinal injury: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — recovery position keeps airway clear; suspected spinal injury requires avoiding movement.

rows.text: Do not automatically raise the legs after a head injury: there may be other injuries. Call emergency services and avoid unnecessary movement, especially if you suspect a spinal injury.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

NHS Wales, First aid, Breathing and spinal injury: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — recovery position keeps airway clear; suspected spinal injury requires avoiding movement.

rows.text: In shock, the circulation does not deliver enough blood and oxygen to vital organs, including the brain and heart. It is an emergency.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock: https://medlineplus.gov/shock.html — insufficient blood and oxygen reach organs; emergency.

rows.text: For shock, a conscious person may be laid on their back with legs raised to help circulation if they have no head, neck, back or leg injury. Call emergency services immediately; do not raise the legs if this causes pain or harm.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: Severe bleeding reduces circulating blood and can prevent organs from receiving enough, causing shock. Emergency help is needed.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help and risk from major bleeding.

rows.text: Confusion can occur in shock because circulation does not supply organs with enough oxygen. It is a sign to take seriously.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: In shock the pulse may be rapid and weak as the body responds to inadequate circulation. Call emergency services immediately.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: A markedly flushed face is not a typical sign of shock: skin may instead be pale, cold and sweaty. Symptoms can vary.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: Blood pressure can fall in shock when circulation fails to supply the organs adequately. If you suspect shock, do not wait for a measurement before calling emergency services.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: A superficial graze alone does not indicate shock. Shock involves inadequate circulation and can follow severe blood loss.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.
Hato Hone St John, Bleeding, Abrasion: https://www.stjohn.org.nz/first-aid/first-aid-library/bleeding/ — care for a superficial graze.

rows.text: Do not give alcohol or other drinks to a person in shock. Call emergency services and help them while waiting.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: The recovery position is not a stimulant for shock: it helps keep the airway clear in an unconscious person who is breathing.
evidence: NHS Wales, First aid, Breathing and spinal injury: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — recovery position keeps airway clear; suspected spinal injury requires avoiding movement.
MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: Continuous shouting alone does not identify shock. Possible signs include pallor, cold sweat, confusion and a rapid, weak pulse.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.

rows.text: Pallor, cold sweaty skin and shivering can accompany shock when circulation is inadequate. Not all symptoms need be present.
evidence: MedlinePlus, Shock, Symptoms and First Aid: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000039.htm — inadequate circulation, symptoms and shock positioning precautions.
NHS Wales, First aid, shock: https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — pale cold clammy skin and shivering are possible signs.

rows.text: Insecticides are not wound treatments. Stop the bleeding and use a clean dressing; clean small wounds once bleeding has stopped.
evidence: NHS, Cuts and grazes: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — stop bleeding, clean and cover wounds; infection risk.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help and risk from major bleeding.

rows.text: Do more than call for help: direct pressure on the wound also helps control venous bleeding. If severe, call emergency services and maintain pressure.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help and risk from major bleeding.

rows.text: The quiz marks this TRUE, but does not say whether it means pressure on the wound or on an artery at a distant pressure point. Current guidance is to call emergency services and promptly apply firm direct pressure to the wound; for severe uncontrolled bleeding follow the dispatcher’s instructions. The usefulness of distant pressure points is uncertain.
evidence: American Heart Association/American Red Cross 2024 First Aid Guidelines, severe external bleeding recommendations 1 and 4, https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines: direct pressure initially; usefulness of indirect manual pressure points uncertain. Volunteer occlusion is not proof of clinical bleeding control.

Resuscitation Council UK 2025 First Aid Guidelines, https://www.resus.org.uk/professional-library/2025-resuscitation-guidelines/first-aid-guidelines: early help, direct pressure and appropriate escalation for life-threatening bleeding; UK emergency number not used as Italian number.

rows.text: The priority is to control bleeding and get help if it is severe: major blood loss can be life-threatening. The priority is not keeping the road clean.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help and risk from major bleeding.

rows.text: Severe arterial bleeding can quickly be fatal. Call emergency services and apply direct pressure to the wound to control blood loss.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help and risk from major bleeding.

rows.text: A wound can become infected. After stopping bleeding, clean small wounds and cover them with a clean dressing; serious wounds need medical attention.
evidence: NHS, Cuts and grazes: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — stop bleeding, clean and cover wounds; infection risk.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help and risk from major bleeding.

review.review_evidence: Independent full review of 25 questions, verdicts and all four current drafts; no figures. AHA/Red Cross 2024 severe bleeding recommendations directly inspected: initial direct pressure and uncertain usefulness of distant pressure points; corrected zh-Hans 31671 accurately says pressure point away from wound. St John Canada exact local PDF SHA256 f8348e9b23433675f6ce88e26482164219c366c7f28182f385cf7aaba1eda583 PDF p159 inspected: do not pack ear, cover lightly with suspected skull fracture. NHS Wales recovery and spine caution, MedlinePlus shock/leg elevation, Red Cross external bleeding and NHS cuts guidance inspected.

issues.reason: Il quesito classifica VERO la compressione dell'arteria principale interessata, senza precisare se si intenda pressione diretta sulla ferita o compressione indiretta a monte. Le indicazioni attuali distinguono i due metodi e sconsigliano i punti di pressione indiretti; non è verificabile quale sia il significato inteso dal testo.
checked_sources: American Red Cross, Focused Updates and Guidelines 2020, First Aid: Direct Pressure, Pressure Dressings, Pressure Points, p. 14: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/course-fact-sheets/American-Red-Cross-Focused-Updates-and-Guidelines-2020-v2.pdf — recommends direct pressure at the bleeding source and advises against indirect pressure points for life-threatening external bleeding.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — instructs firm direct pressure on the wound and emergency help.

source_access_notes: Independently inspected AHA/American Red Cross 2024 first aid severe bleeding recommendations: direct wound pressure first; usefulness of indirect pressure points uncertain; tourniquet for uncontrolled life-threatening extremity bleeding. Inspected MedlinePlus shock first aid (conditional leg elevation and injury precautions), NHS Wales first-aid spinal and airway guidance, and St John ear-injury guidance. English, Italian and Spanish 31671 retain direct/indirect distinction.
